lesson.title: Speeding Up or Slowing Down? Comparing Velocity and Acceleration
lesson.summary: An object speeds up when velocity and acceleration share the same sign and slows down when their signs are opposite, a rule that follows directly from combining direction of motion with acceleration.
lesson.body:
Knowing acceleration alone doesn't tell you whether an object is speeding up or slowing down. Negative acceleration, for instance, could mean an object moving forward is decelerating, or it could mean an object already moving backward is speeding up in that backward direction. The only way to tell which is happening is to compare the sign of acceleration to the sign of velocity at that same instant, combining the last two chapters directly.

When v(t) and a(t) have the same sign, both positive or both negative, the object is speeding up: acceleration is reinforcing the direction of motion. When v(t) and a(t) have opposite signs, the object is slowing down: acceleration is fighting against the direction of motion. When a(t) = 0, speed is momentarily neither increasing nor decreasing.

Return one final time to s(t) = t^3 - 6t^2 + 9t, with v(t) = 3(t - 1)(t - 3) and a(t) = 6(t - 2). Check four representative instants. At t = 0.5: v(0.5) = 3(-0.5)(-2.5) = 3.75 (positive), and a(0.5) = 6(0.5) - 12 = -9 (negative); opposite signs, so the object is slowing down. At t = 1.5: v(1.5) = 3(0.5)(-1.5) = -2.25 (negative), and a(1.5) = 6(1.5) - 12 = -3 (negative); same sign, so the object is speeding up, in the negative direction. At t = 2.5: v(2.5) = 3(1.5)(-0.5) = -2.25 (negative), and a(2.5) = 6(2.5) - 12 = 3 (positive); opposite signs, so the object is slowing down again. At t = 4: v(4) = 9 (positive), and a(4) = 12 (positive); same sign, so the object is speeding up.

Putting every chapter in this unit together, here is the complete account of this object's motion. From t = 0 to t = 1, it moves forward while slowing down, coming to rest at t = 1. From t = 1 to t = 2, it moves backward while speeding up, reaching its fastest backward speed right at t = 2, exactly where a(t) = 0. From t = 2 to t = 3, it's still moving backward but now slowing down, coming to rest again at t = 3. From t = 3 onward, it moves forward while speeding up. Every one of those descriptions, forward or backward, speeding up or slowing down, comes directly from comparing the signs of v(t) and a(t), the same two functions built by differentiating position, twice, at the very start of this unit.
